summary: Desktop chat app for running your own team of AI bots, each a real Claude or Codex agent with its own model, apps and computer.

heroCommands.command: Get the macOS, Windows or Linux build from the latest release

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OpenMausBot is an open-source, local-first chat app where every bot in the sidebar is a real agent, powered by Claude or Codex running locally. Each bot has its own personality, model, computer and connected apps. You talk to them like contacts, watch them work and approve important actions. Teams of bots can be installed from a portable Markdown file.
sixtySeconds.problem: Running several AI agents for different jobs usually means juggling terminals. OpenMausBot puts them in one chat-style app with approvals and channels.
whoFor: People who want a personal team of AI agents
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it to bring your own agent and existing logins, with bots that ask before they act, channels, routines and an MCP interface.
requirements: macOS, Windows x64, Ubuntu 24.04 x64 or Fedora x64
An existing Claude, ChatGPT/Codex or Grok login

overview: Download the released build for your platform; the harness server is built in, so there's nothing else to set up. Builds for macOS are signed and notarized; the Windows installer needs no admin rights.
Pick a model per bot, connect apps, and organize bots into channels. Imported teams arrive with connections off and routines paused until you approve them.
Bots can be orchestrated over MCP or from scripts, and one computer's bots can be opened from another over Tailscale. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.

features.title: Bot team
features.body: Each bot is a real agent.

limitations: Lots of moving parts for beginners

install.verificationNote: Commands come from OpenMausBot's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Download
steps.body: Get OpenMausBot.dmg (Apple silicon) or OpenMausBot-intel.dmg from the latest release.

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Drag it to Applications and open it.

steps.title: Run the installer
steps.body: Download OpenMausBot-setup.exe and run it; no admin rights needed.

steps.title: Install the package
steps.body: Use the .deb or AppImage on Ubuntu 24.04, or the .rpm on Fedora (sudo dnf install ./OpenMausBot-x86_64.rpm from your Downloads folder).

firstRun.title: Connect a brain
firstRun.body: Sign in with Claude, ChatGPT/Codex or add an xAI key for Grok.

firstRun.title: Message a bot
firstRun.body: Talk to it like a contact.

tutorial.title: Install a ready-made bot team
tutorial.useCase: Import a team from a Markdown playbook.

steps.title: Find a team
steps.body: Browse teams on BotMRR and choose Add to OpenMausBot, or use Teams, Import with a file or GitHub URL.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: Check the bots, channels and connector checklist on the review screen.

steps.title: Turn things on
steps.body: Approve connections and unpause routines you want.

tutorial.expected: A set of bots and channels ready to work, with nothing enabled until you approve it.
